title: nvme-mi: Fix request/response tracking and add MPR support
description:
The original dissector stored request/response state directly in the
per-conversation nvme_mi_command struct and mutated it on every
dissection pass.  This caused three problems:

1. On re-dissection, the request frame was processed before its
   response, so resp_frame was zero or stale — response_in showed
   the wrong frame or nothing at all.

2. No pinfo->fd->visited guard protected the conversation state, so
   re-dissection clobbered the mappings established on the first pass.

3. The dissector treated every command slot as a single request/response
   pair, ignoring the NVMe-MI "More Processing Required" (MPR) status
   that allows interim responses before the final one.

Fix all three by introducing per-frame data (p_add_proto_data) with a
shared nvme_mi_transaction pointer.  The transaction is allocated once
per request and shared across all frames in that exchange, so the
request frame sees resp_frame as soon as it is written during the
response's first-pass dissection — no second pass needed.

All conversation-side mutation is now guarded by !pinfo->fd->visited.
MPR interim responses (status byte 0x01) keep the command slot open;
only the final response closes it and records resp_frame.

Add hf_nvme_mi_response_is_mpr display filter field for MPR responses.

Closes #21269

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)
